segmenti.tekst: …a person will not taste the sweetness of iman (faith) until Allah and His Messenger are dearest to him.

And how will a person make Allah and His Messenger dearest to him? By getting to know, of course, Allah and His Messenger: Allah through His attributes, or qualities, and the Messenger through his sirah (biography).
The first thing a person should know in relation to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is to believe in Allah's lordship. What does this mean – that a person believes in Allah's lordship?

That he believes that Allah is the only true Lord. Several things are included in this. The first thing is that a person believes that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is free from and exalted above what the unbelievers attribute to Him,

what the unbelievers among the Christians, the Jews and the mushrikun (idolaters) attribute to Him. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "The Originator of the heavens and the Earth." See how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, begins the ayah:
"Badi'us-samawati wal-ard" – the Originator of the heavens and the Earth – "anna yakunu lahu waladun wa lam takun lahu sahibah" – He says: how could He have a child when He has no wife?

How could He have a child when He has no wife? "Wa khalaqa kulla shay'in wa huwa bi kulli shay'in 'alim" – and He created everything, and He knows everything. We know that the Christians and the Jews attribute a child to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala,
as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions in the Qur'an. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ" – and the Jews say: Uzayr is the son of Allah.

Uzayr – who is Uzayr? Uzayr was a good man; some say he was a prophet. And Uzayr, well, Uzayr had memorised the Tawrah (Torah), just as we memorise the Qur'an today. The only one who had memorised the Tawrah.

So some of the Jews, [unclear], said, they said: he is the son of Allah. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: "وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ" – and the Christians say, the Christians say: Isa is the son of Allah.
ذَٰلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ
segmenti.prevod: “That is their saying with their mouths…” (At-Tawbah 9:30)

segmenti.tekst: That is only, that is only their saying, from their own whims. This saying resembles the saying of the unbelievers before them.

"Qatalahumullahu anna yu'fakun" – may Allah destroy them, how they are deluded! So we see how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, begins the ayah above, saying: "Badi'us-samawati wal-ard" – the Originator of the heavens and the Earth. Does the Originator of the heavens and the Earth, dear brothers, the One who created the heavens and the Earth, need to have a child or a wife?
That would indicate a deficiency, an imperfection, and Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is free from that. How, how dangerous, dear brothers, is what the Jews, the Christians and the mushrikun say!

Pay attention to the ayat that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions in the Qur'an. He says: "وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا" – and they say, He says: Allah has taken a child for Himself, that is, Allah the Most Merciful has a child. "Wa qalut-takhadhar-Rahmanu walada, laqad ji'tum shay'an idda" –
you have come with a monstrous thing; what you say is a monstrous thing. "Takadus-samawatu yatafattarna minhu" – He says: the heavens almost burst apart –

"wa tanshaqqul-ardu" – and the earth almost split open – "wa takhirrul-jibalu hadda" – and the mountains almost crumbled. Why? Why all of this? Why, dear brothers? He says: "An da'aw lir-Rahmani walada" –

because they attributed a child to Allah, that is, they say that Allah has a child. See how dangerous a word that is! "Wa ma yanbaghi lir-Rahmani an yattakhidha walada" – and, He says, it is not befitting for Allah to take a child.
Allah, Allah has no need of that. So this, dear brothers, is a warning – here, their holidays have just been – to those who congratulate our Orthodox neighbours on their holidays.
How dangerous that is, dear brothers! That is, this is directly connected to [unclear]. No one forbids us from treating them well, from helping them if we are able, and so on.

But to congratulate them on Easter – and let whoever is interested in what Easter means, that is, and Christmas, go back and look – let him see how closely it is connected to a person's belief. That because of that saying the heavens almost came crashing down on us, the earth almost split in half, and the mountains almost crumbled.

Because of this saying. And then a person comes along after this and congratulates them on their holidays. Also, also, Abdullah ibn Abbas mentions, in a hadith recorded by Bukhari, that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), said: Allah says: "Kadhdhabani ibnu Adama wa lam yakun lahu dhalik" – the son of Adam lies about Me, and he has no right to do so – "wa shatamani wa lam yakun lahu dhalik" – and he insults Me, and he has no right to do so.
He says: as for his denying Me, it is his saying that I cannot bring him back as he was,

that is, that I cannot bring him back to life. So, how dangerous, dangerous, dangerous it is for a person to say that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will not, will not bring people back to life again. He further says: "wa amma shatmuhu iyyaya" – He says: and as for his insulting Me, it is his saying that I have a child.
That I have a child. Glorified and exalted am I above taking, or having, a child or a wife.

You see, dear brothers, how the hadiths and the ayat tell us everything. They tell us everything. You also know that the mushrikun in the time of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, used to say that the angels were the daughters of Allah.

That they were the daughters of Allah. And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ الْبَنَاتِ … وَلَهُمْ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ" – and, He says, these mushrikun attribute… to themselves, that is, "wa yaj'aluna lillahil-banati" – they attribute daughters to Allah – "wa lahum ma yashtahun" – and to themselves what they love: sons. They loved sons, they… daughters. "Wa idha bushshira ahaduhum bil-untha" – and, He says, when one of them is told that he has had a daughter – "zalla wajhuhu muswaddan wa huwa kazim" –

He says: his face turns black with grief. That is why among us people say: "Look, he's gone black in the face," from grief, from pain. And that is what they were like: when news came that he had had a daughter, He says, his face would turn black with grief. "Zalla wajhuhu muswaddan wa huwa kazim.
Yatawara minal-qawmi min su'i ma bushshira bih" – He says: he hides from the people, so that they would not mock him because of what he had been given, that is, because he had had a daughter.
أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرَابِ
segmenti.prevod: “…should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust?” (An-Nahl 16:59)

segmenti.tekst: He says: should he keep that daughter and be humiliated his whole life, mocked by his people? He says: how evil is their judgement! How evil is their judgement and how they divide!
How evil is their judgement and their dividing. Also, also, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says – addressing the mushrikun, He says: "Is it that for you," He says, you attribute sons,

"and for Him" – for Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – daughters? So with these ayat and hadiths Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, denies, denies, denies that He has a child, or a wife, or daughters, or daughters.

That is why it is very important for a person to know his creed – we mentioned this a little earlier – so that it does not come to a person, Allah forbid, leaving this religion through such actions. Also, what a person should believe is that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only Creator of everything, of everything that exists.

In Surah Al-An'am, from the 95th ayah to the 106th ayah, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions that He is the One who gives life and death, that He is the One who created the sun and the moon so that people could reckon time,
that He is the One who created the stars so that people could find their way. What did the Arabs do back then? They would travel by night and rest by day, because it is cooler at night than by day.
So they would travel and then find their way by the stars: the North Star, north. And here Allah mentions how He provided, or gave, or created the stars so that people could find their way by them.

Allah also mentions – in these ayat – that He created us from one man, from Adam. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, also mentions that He is the One who sends down rain from the sky, which reaches the earth, and from the earth there then grow various fruits and vegetables with which man feeds himself.

What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say at the end of these ayat? "Dhalikumullahu Rabbukum" – this is your Lord. "Dhalikumullahu Rabbukum" – this is Allah, your Lord. Does the One who did all of this, who created it, not deserve to be worshipped? "Dhalikumullahu Rabbukum, la ilaha illa huwa" – there is no deity worthy of worship except Him. "Dhalikumullahu Rabbukum, la ilaha illa huwa, khaliqu kulli shay'in fa'buduh" – the Creator of everything, so worship Him.

So with these ayat Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, tells us clearly, clearly that He is the Creator, the Creator of everything. Also, Abu Hurayrah, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu, narrates in this "Sahih" of Bukhari that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: Allah said: "وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ ذَهَبَ يَخْلُقُ كَخَلْقِي" – He says: who is more unjust than the one who sets out to create something like what I have created? What is meant here is making images – for those who make images of living beings.

It is narrated that Abu Hurayrah, when he quoted this hadith, had entered the house of Marwan ibn al-Hakam. Marwan ibn al-Hakam was the governor of Medina in the time of Mu'awiyah. He entered his house and saw a painter painting living beings on the walls of that house.

And he said, that is, he quoted this hadith. This hadith clearly, clearly forbids making images of living, living beings. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: "فَلْيَخْلُقُوا ذَرَّةً" – so, He says, let them create, let them create a single speck.

Let a person, if he can, create a single speck, a single atom. "فَلْيَخْلُقُوا حَبَّةً" – He says: let a person, if he can, create a single grain. "Falyakhluqu sha'iratan" – and let him create a single grain of barley.
Why does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mention grains here? Why, dear brothers? Because when you take this grain, put it in the ground and water it, something living will sprout from that grain:

either wheat, or barley, or this, or that, depending on what a person plants. So these ayat – and there are many ayat saying that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only Creator of everything – so it is upon the believer to believe that there is no creator other than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
Also, what a person should believe is that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only One who gives life and death. That Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only One who gives life, life and death.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "He is the One who gives life and death, and to Him you will, to Him you will return." To Him you will, to Him you will return. You know the story of when Ibrahim, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him), argued with Nimrod.

And Nimrod was the ruler of Babylon, as the mufassirun (Qur'an commentators) say. This Nimrod was extremely arrogant, a great tyrant; he said of himself that he was lord. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Alam tara ilal-ladhi hajja Ibrahima fi Rabbihi an atahullahul-mulk."

He says: have you not seen the one who argued with Ibrahim, alayhis-salam, after Allah had given him kingship? "Idh qala Ibrahimu Rabbiyal-ladhi yuhyi wa yumit" – when Ibrahim, alayhis-salam, said to him:
"My Lord is the One, my Lord gives life and death." And this Nimrod said: "No, rather I give life and death." And then, in the next sentence, Ibrahim… how he refuted those claims of his!
He said: "Very well, if you claim that you are lord – Allah makes the sun come, or rise, from the east.

So you, if you claim to be lord, make the sun rise, make the sun come, rise from the west." And he says… this is why, as our people would say, he sealed his mouth. He could not speak any more, any more. This clearly shows that Allah is the One who gives life and death. There is an interesting narration from Abu Hurayrah, recorded by both Bukhari and Muslim in their "Sahih" collections: he says that there was a man from the Children of Israel, from the Jews, before Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, who believed in Allah,

did not commit shirk against Him, that is, did not ascribe partners to Him, nor did he worship anyone besides Allah. But, he says, despite that, he says, he never did any good, that is, he believed in Allah but did no good at all. And before he passed away – what happens? He left a will for his sons, his descendants, saying: "When I die, take me, burn me, and that ash – one part," he says, "throw into the sea, let the sea swallow it, and the other part," he says, "leave on some height, so that

the wind will scatter it." And he passed away. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, informs us, he says: he will come on the Day of Judgement, and Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will command the sea to gather the part that was thrown into the sea.
And the earth will be commanded to gather the part that was thrown on the land. And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will bring him back to life, He will bring him back to life again from nothing.

And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will say to him: "Why did you do this?" What does this man say to Him? He says: "Out of fear of You. I was afraid. I worshipped You, my Lord, but I never," he says, "did any good." And Allah says to him: "You are forgiven." And Allah, he says, will forgive him.
Why? Because he worshipped Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, alone. A person thinks that Allah will not bring him back to life. He says: "Does man think that We will not," He says, "gather his bones?

Yes indeed, We are," He says, "able to restore even his fingertips," to create them again as they were. Allah says in another ayah: "كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ" – He says: just as He created you… For Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, created us from nothing.

We came into being from nothing. He says: "ta'udun" – you will be: just as He created you the first time, so He will create you again. So, it is logical; it could not be more logical. Also, what a person should believe, and it is a very important thing: that he believes that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only One who gives provision and the only One who knows when a person's ajal (appointed term) will come.

The only One who gives provision, the only One who records for a person – or it has been recorded for every person by Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – when his ajal will come, when his ajal will come. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "He created you from clay."

What is clay? Clay is earth mixed with water. That is, Allah created your father Adam from clay. "Thumma qada ajalan" – and then He prescribed, or recorded, for each of you when death would come to him.

He recorded for each of you when death would come to him. "وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ" – and He also recorded when, when the Day of Judgement will come. So we see clearly here, dear brothers, that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the One who determines, or records, when a person's ajal will come. And imagine if one of us now knew when his death would come –
surely, surely he would go mad within a few hours. But it is part of Allah's wisdom that a person does not know when his death will come, thanks be to Allah. "Wa ma tadri nafsun bi ayyi ardin tamut."

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: and a person does not know, He says, in which land he will die. "Wa ma tadri nafsun madha taksibu ghada" – and He says: a person does not know, He says, what he will earn tomorrow, what awaits him tomorrow. None of us knows what awaits us tomorrow.

No one knows what awaits us in an hour's time and so on; he does not know what comes in a minute. "Wa ma tadri nafsun bi ayyi ardin tamut" – He says: a person does not know in which, He says, land. How many times does it happen to people – believe me, there are people who travel to New Zealand just to visit their son for a while, and pass away there; a person goes on umrah, passes away there and is buried in Mecca. So, a person does not know in which place he will pass away. It is part of Allah's wisdom that a person does not know.

Also, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا" – and He says: there is no living creature in this world that Allah does not provide for. There is no living creature in this world that Allah does not provide for. Only Allah gives rizq (provision). Today in the hutba (Friday sermon) I spoke about… [unclear] when a person says: "I did this," he says, "with my own ten fingers."

What did you do with your ten fingers? How many times, by Allah, does a person strive, and there is no rizq; sometimes something small, and there it is, rizq from Allah. And believe me, dear brothers, rizq, or provision, is not tied to a person's intelligence or a person's cleverness.

You will see that someone who is very clever has little. And you will see someone who is less clever… that is, the one who is very clever has little, very little; you will see him living modestly. And the one who is little… who is not particularly clever, he has a lot, he has millions. So, rizq, or provision, is not tied to a person's cleverness or a person's intelligence.

That is what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gives people: to some He gives more, to some less; to some He gives more with less effort, and to some He gives less with much effort. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gives this to people out of His mercy.

The scholars say: three things, they say, destroy a person. One of those three things, they say, is money. Perhaps Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, knows that the one who is very clever, intelligent, a good believer – perhaps, if money came to him, he might abandon the religion and everything.

So Allah knows, and out of His wisdom, why He gives some people less and some, some more. He says: "Wa ma min dabbatin fil-ardi illa 'alallahi rizquha wa ya'lamu mustaqarraha wa mustawda'aha" – He says: there is no living creature in this world that Allah does not provide for,

and He knows the place where it will die, and how it will die, and when it will die. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, knows all of that. "Kullun fi kitabin mubin" – He says: everything is recorded in al-Lawh al-Mahfuz, the Preserved Tablet.

Carefully preserved, 50,000 years before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, created the heavens and the Earth. Imagine! So our destinies were recorded 50,000 years before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, created the heavens and the Earth. Also, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Allahul-ladhi khalaqakum" –

He says: truly, Allah created you. Allah created us from nothing. "Thumma razaqakum" – so, Allah created us, we came into this world with nothing, as our people would say: naked and barefoot. "Thumma razaqakum" – and then He provided for you, and Allah provided for us.

"Thumma yumitukum" – then He will take the soul, a person will die. "Thumma yuhyikum" – and then He will bring you back to life, to give, to give an account. "Hal min shuraka'ikum man yaf'alu min dhalikum min shay'?"

He now addresses them, He says, He says: "Can any of these false deities of yours do anything like this?" Can they? How Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, refutes their claims! Can those false deities of yours, those idols, those shrines that are worshipped and prayed to even today,

can they do anything like this? They cannot, dear brothers. And that is why a person should worship Allah alone. That is why a person should worship Allah alone, not worship anyone besides Him, nor think that anyone can benefit him or harm him

except Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. In a hadith narrated by Anas ibn Malik, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu, and recorded by Bukhari – you see, here we only quote hadiths from Bukhari and Muslim, so that no one comes and says: "Oh, efendi, you're quoting us hadiths [unclear]," or this, or that, and so on –

the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Innallaha 'azza wa jalla wakkala bir-rahimi malakan." He says: truly Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has appointed an angel in charge of a woman's womb.

And this angel says: "Ya Rabbi, nutfah." When the seed reaches the womb, this angel says: "My Lord, the seed has arrived." That is the first stage of man's creation: the seed, when it reaches the womb.

Then when the second stage comes, the second stage comes, he says: "Ya Rabbi, 'alaqah." He says: "My Lord, 'alaqah" – and 'alaqah means a clot, or a small lump of blood. That is the second stage of man's creation.

The second stage, well, of man's creation. 'Alaqah means something that clings: that little lump attaches itself to the woman's womb. Then when a little time comes, a little time passes, he says: "Ya Rabbi, mudghah."

Mudghah is a piece of flesh. So, already the third stage of man's creation, already the third stage of man's creation. He further says: "Fa idha arada an yaqdiya khalqahu" – the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: and when, before the creation of the person in his mother's womb is completed, that angel says to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala: "A dhakarun am untha?" –

he says: will it be male or female? "A shaqiyyun am sa'id?" – will it be happy or wretched? What does happy or wretched mean? Whether it will be among the people of Jannah (Paradise) or Jahannam (Hellfire). "Fariqun fil-jannati wa fariqun fis-sa'ir" – He says: one group will be in Jannah, and the other in the Fire.

Dear brothers, while still in the womb it will be recorded [unclear]: whether he will be among the people of Jannah or Jahannam. He says: "Fama ar-rizqu wal-ajal?" – he says: there will be recorded for him – imagine – his provision; in his mother's womb his provision will be recorded for him,

how much provision he will have in this world – "wal-ajal" – and, he says, when death will come to him. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, records these things for a person while he is still in his mother's womb:
whether the person will be a man or a woman, whether he will be among the people of Jannah or Jahannam, how much his provision will be and when death will come to him.

So a person should believe that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only One who gives provision and the only One who determines the appointed time, or the moment, when death will come to him. And the last thing connected with this lordship of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, or the belief that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only Lord, who created us, who gave us rizq, and so on and so on and so forth, is that a person believes that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the only One who governs the universe and everything that exists.

We see that there are quite a few groups that ascribe themselves to Islam but are mushrikun, who say, I don't know: Ali is the one who, a'udhu billah, governs the universe; that, I don't know… the Christians say: Jesus is the one who governs the universe. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, refutes their claims, saying that He is the One who governs the universe and everything that exists.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says – and see how Allah begins the ayah – He says: "Qul man yarzuqukum minas-sama'i wal-ard" – say, say, O Messenger: who is it that provides for you from the sky – sends rain down to you, rain – "wal-ard" – and from the Earth, so that plants, fruits and vegetables grow from it? "Qul man yarzuqukum minas-sama'i wal-ard, amman yamlikus-sam'a wal-absar" – He says: who is it that owns your hearing and sight? See how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, goes a little further and mentions hearing and sight. He says: who is it that owns your hearing and sight?

Why does Allah mention hearing and sight? Why did He not mention the hand, the foot, and so on? Because hearing and sight, besides guidance, are the greatest, the greatest blessings of Allah. Would any of you give up your sight for all the wealth on this earth? Certainly not. Your hearing? Certainly not, certainly not. That is why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions hearing and sight here, hearing and sight, which people enjoy, enjoy those blessings. "Wa man yukhrijul-hayya minal-mayyiti

wa yukhrijul-mayyita minal-hayy" – He says: who is it that brings forth the living from the lifeless, so that from the wheat, or from that grain, He makes sprout, makes sprout an ear, a living ear; and the reverse, who is it that brings forth the lifeless from the living – so Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, makes the wheat come out, come out of that ear. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: and, He says, who is it that governs everything?

And they will say… they will surely answer you, they will surely answer that it is Allah. Why will they answer that it is Allah? Why did the mushrikun say that it is Allah? He says, he says, this… Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in the Qur'an: "Wa la'in sa'altahum man khalaqas-samawati wal-arda la-yaqulunnallah" – He says: and if you were to ask them who created the heavens and the Earth, they would say: "It is Allah." So the mushrikun believed that Allah created the heavens and the Earth, but they had a problem with other things, which we will mention, in sha Allah, which we will mention in the next lecture. Allah says:

"Do you not fear Allah's punishment?" You know all these things, yet you do not worship Him. You know that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the One who gives life and death, you know that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the One who owns your hearing and sight, you know that Allah is the One who governs everything, and despite that you do not worship Him, despite that you do not prostrate to Him – a big problem.

It is also narrated in a hadith narrated by Anas ibn Malik and recorded, of course, by Bukhari and Muslim; Anas says: the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam – since we, he says, asked him a lot, we asked him a great deal – he says, forbade us from asking him.

Why? The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: the earlier ummahs, or earlier nations, were destroyed because they asked their prophets too many questions. Like today: we have people who come to ask the efendi – believe me, sometimes he knows the answer, but he only comes to ask the efendi to see where the efendi stands, which way he leans, whose side he is on, to test him, to see that he is not one of those who are for [unclear], and so on.

So the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, forbade, forbade the companions from asking too much, since that was one of the causes for which past nations were destroyed. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "O you who believe," He says, "do not," He says, "ask about things which, if they were made plain to you, would displease you."

Rather, a person should ask about what he truly does not know and what truly concerns him, and of course what is beneficial to him. And you have people who ask, ask about everything, ask about things that they will never need in their lives.

A person should ask, that is, about what he needs for his religion, for his religion; and as for worldly matters, let him not ask the efendi, but let him ask someone else. And this… Anas ibn Malik says: "So we," he says, "longed for one of the Bedouins, the Bedouins, to come and ask the Prophet something."

"So," he says, "when one of the Bedouins," he says, "would come" – and the Bedouins, he says, were very sharp and clever – "we would," he says, "gather," he says, "around the Prophet to hear what he would ask him, to hear what he would ask him." "For," he says, "we had been forbidden," but this prohibition had not reached them; they had not heard of this prohibition.

And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did not want to send them away, because a man would come 500 kilometres, 1,000 kilometres from Medina – how could the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, send him away? Rather, the Prophet would answer him, answer his question. So this Bedouin came, he says, and asked the Prophet, saying: "Your envoy came to me, your envoy came to me, claiming that you are a messenger."

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "He spoke the truth; I am the Messenger." Now, see here what we were talking about a little earlier, He says: if you were to ask these Arabs who created the heavens and the Earth, He says, they would say, they would say: "Allah." See the conversation between, between the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and this Bedouin.

The Bedouin says: "O Muhammad," he says, "who created the heavens?" The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Allah created them." He said: "Who created the Earth?" The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Allah created the Earth." "And who," he said, "set up, or who made these mountains to be pillars holding the Earth, so that the Earth would not shake?"

The Prophet said: "Allah. It is Allah." This Bedouin says… so this Bedouin confirms that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the Creator of all that. But what does he want from the Prophet? That the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, bear witness, that is, he asks the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, to swear an oath,

to swear an oath. This Bedouin says: "Fa billadhi khalaqas-sama'a wa khalaqal-arda wa nasaba hadhihil-jibal…" He says: "By the One," he says, "who created the heavens, the Earth and these mountains," he says, "are you truly a messenger?"

The Prophet said: "Yes, I am truly, truly, truly the Messenger." So we see from this, dear brothers, that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – that is, according to the words of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and His own words that He mentions in the Qur'an – is the One who governs, governs everything.

That He is the One who created the heavens, who governs the heavens, who governs the Earth, who governs the mountains. And a person, a Muslim, a Muslim, a Muslim, should believe in all of this. And these, believe me, are, so to say, the most important – no – among the most important things, we can say the most important things, as far as a person's, a person's belief is concerned.

We ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to reward you with every, every good, for listening attentively, for coming this evening to spend time together here and learn about Allah's religion. And I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins and the sins of our parents, and to bring us together in Jannah. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin.
